title: COP31: Rebuilding the Loss and Damage Fund for speed
gist: Ojha and Adhikari argue the UN Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) has a delivery problem as much as a size problem: its first decisive act, a US$21.6m set-aside for Nepal's August glacial flood, took 57 days and still hasn't disbursed, while parametric pools (Jamaica's cat bond, Vanuatu's insurer) pay in about two weeks. They urge COP31 in Antalya to reposition the FRLD as a hub that capitalises pre-triggered regional pools, with 14-day and 90-day delivery deadlines.

insights.claim: On 22 October the FRLD board set aside US$21.6 million for Nepal after a 26 August glacial flood in the Bhotekoshi valley killed more than 1,500 people and left over 5,000 missing — its first approval after four years of approving nothing.
insights.speaker: Hemant Ojha
entities: Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage
insights.so_what: Benchmark for how slowly multilateral climate loss finance reaches disaster zones.

insights.claim: The Nepal set-aside took 57 days, no money has moved, no implementing organisation has been chosen because Nepal cannot apply directly, and by the next board meeting in Manila on 15 December the flood will be 111 days old.
insights.speaker: Hemant Ojha
insights.so_what: Indicates multilateral loss-and-damage cash is effectively unavailable for immediate response.
insights.quote: But it took 57 days, and the money has still not moved.

insights.claim: In July the FRLD board deferred its first package of four grants worth US$77.4 million until December, and its start-up disbursement target slipped from mid-2026 to year's end.
insights.speaker: Hemant Ojha
entities: Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage

insights.claim: The FRLD board has 26 members, meets about three times a year, decides by consensus and appraises requests one at a time, creating governance bottlenecks money alone cannot fix.
insights.speaker: Hemant Ojha
entities: Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage
insights.so_what: Institutional design, not just funding, is the binding constraint.
insights.quote: A fund ten times larger, built this way, could still make a flood wait for a quorum.
insights.locator: The campaign to replenish the Fund

insights.claim: The FRLD has US$822 million pledged and about US$450 million paid in, against 176 requests worth about US$2.8 billion.
insights.speaker: Hemant Ojha
entities: Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage
insights.so_what: Pledge-to-payment gap of ~45% shows weak donor follow-through.
insights.locator: The Fund is short of money

insights.claim: The US$342 million reserved for the FRLD's first round covers roughly one-eighth of requests, while a peer-reviewed estimate puts annual loss and damage needs near US$400 billion.
insights.speaker: Hemant Ojha
entities: Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage
insights.so_what: Gap of three orders of magnitude implies large structural demand for alternative risk-transfer (insurance, cat bonds).
insights.locator: The Fund is short of money

themes.theme: Parametric and regional models work faster

insights.claim: Jamaica's regional risk pool and catastrophe bond were due to pay US$242 million within 16 days of Hurricane Melissa, and Vanuatu's regional insurer paid within 14 days of its 2024 earthquake, because rules, triggers and payment channels were agreed in advance.
insights.speaker: Hemant Ojha
insights.so_what: Validates sovereign cat bonds and parametric risk pools as the fast-payout channel — a growth area for ILS markets.
insights.quote: The rules, triggers and payment channels had been agreed in advance.

insights.claim: The FRLD should not manage every payment itself but pool finance, set common rules for triggers, tracking and audit, strengthen national systems and channel cash via risk pools, social protection systems and bodies such as the Pacific Resilience Facility.
insights.speaker: Hemant Ojha
entities: Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage
insights.so_what: If adopted, FRLD capital could flow into regional pools and parametric instruments, expanding that market.
insights.locator: The Fund should learn from them.

insights.claim: Different losses need tiered responses: pre-triggered cash within days, larger recovery grants over months, and multi-year programmes for slow-onset losses like drought and displacement, where the authors' four-country research suggests the FRLD adds most distinctive value.
insights.speaker: Hemant Ojha
entities: Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage
insights.so_what: Slow-onset loss is the FRLD's niche — distinct from insurance-style instruments.
insights.locator: The Fund should learn from them.

insights.claim: Rapid finance should reach countries within 14 days of a declared sudden-onset disaster and recovery grants should be decided within about 90 days; the FRLD currently publishes no measure of how long support takes.
insights.speaker: Hemant Ojha
entities: Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage
insights.so_what: Watch for COP31 adoption of delivery deadlines as a reform signal.
insights.quote: Without them, speed remains an aspiration rather than a requirement.

themes.theme: COP31 reform agenda and Australia/Canada role

insights.claim: Australia's support for the island-owned Pacific Resilience Facility and the Canada-CARICOM Climate Adaptation Fund show how regional institutions can pool risk, subsidise access and release finance quickly.
insights.speaker: Hemant Ojha
insights.so_what: Regional vehicles are candidates for scaled FRLD capital.

insights.claim: COP31 in Antalya should begin repositioning the FRLD from a project fund into the coordinating hub of a broader loss and damage finance system working with regional funds, risk pools, social protection and national institutions under shared standards.
insights.speaker: Hemant Ojha
entities: Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage
insights.so_what: Structural shift in climate-finance architecture to watch at COP31.
insights.quote: reposition it from a project fund into the coordinating hub of a broader loss and damage finance system

insights.claim: The loss and damage debate has focused on scale, but without a delivery focus the world may create a loss and damage fund while failing to create a loss and damage finance system.
insights.speaker: Hemant Ojha
entities: Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage
insights.so_what: Replenishment headlines alone overstate effective support to vulnerable states.
insights.quote: the world may succeed in creating a loss and damage fund while failing to create a loss and damage finance system
insights.locator: The debate over loss and damage
